- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in recent 3–5 days), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60–65), model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of gradual upward correction.  
- When sentiment turns positive (e.g., +0.20+ in last 3 days), model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates true price at end of period; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final forecast to account for momentum.
